title: Quadratic Chirp 26-Layer Stack with Constrained Perturbation Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A quadratic chirp profile in layer optical thicknesses, targeting constructive interference across 300-450 nm while maintaining quarter-wave matching at 1350 nm center SWIR wavelength, will achieve higher dual-band spectral separation than the previous 24-layer designs when optimization is constrained to ±12% perturbations around the chirp baseline.
design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflector with quadratic thickness progression: UV reflection band benefits from chirped layer pairs that span the 300-450 nm stopband, while SWIR transmission is preserved by maintaining approximate quarter-wave optical thickness at 1350 nm. Two-phase optimization prevents solver from breaking the monotonic chirp structure.
proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2/SiO2)_13 | Fused Silica substrate - 26 finite layers total, alternating high/low index starting with HfO2
design_variables: 26 layer thicknesses initialized from quadratic chirp formula, optimized with ±12% bound constraints
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maintain smooth spectral transition between bands
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds prevent extreme values that challenge deposition control
Alternating H/L sequence simplifies process monitoring
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Chirped Bragg reflector theory for broadband reflection
expected_advantages: Quadratic chirp provides broader UV stopband than linear chirp
Constrained optimization preserves physical chirp structure
26 layers offers more degrees of freedom than previous 24-layer attempts without exceeding fabrication limit
known_risks: Constrained optimization may not find global optimum if baseline chirp is poorly chosen
Increased layer count may reduce SWIR transmission due to cumulative absorption/scatter
Quadratic chirp parameters require careful selection for target dispersion
execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 26-layer planar dielectric multilayer coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: HfO2 (high index) and SiO2 (low index), alternating sequence starting with HfO2 adjacent to air. Initialize layer thicknesses using quadratic chirp formula: d_i = d_0 * (1 + alpha * (i-1)^2) where d_0 = 75 nm for HfO2 layers and 110 nm for SiO2 layers, alpha = 0.003. Then perform gradient-based thickness optimization with bound constraints: each thickness may vary ±12% from its initialized value. Wavelength range: 300-1700 nm with 5 nm sampling. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Objective: maximize weighted spectral performance score with equal weight on (1) average reflectance in 300-450 nm band and (2) average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band. Report best candidate thicknesses, target score, robustness score, and full spectral curves. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: reflection in 1000-1700 nm; transmission in 300-450 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum total layer count of 30.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive for two-phase initialization with quadratic chirp baseline and ±12% constrained optimization. Increases layer count from 24 to 26 to provide additional degrees of freedom while staying within 30-layer manufacturing constraint. Addresses score regression by changing initialization strategy rather than repeating previous 24-layer chirped approach.
